# Counters

Every counter Cavalry has, from `counters.toml`, the single source ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-lay-out-the-counters-file.md)). The driver publishes each one in the [counters file](counters-file.md). A static counter is allocated when the file is created, in the record whose index is its id, and its label is its name. An instance counter is allocated per key when its instance is created, and its label is the name, a space, and the key's text as the doc column defines it. A `counter` never decreases while allocated; a `gauge` moves both ways. This page is generated by `scripts/gen-counters.py`: edit `counters.toml`, never this page, and `just lint-counters` fails when the two differ.

| Id | Name | Kind | Scope | What a change means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `counters.allocated` | gauge | static | Metadata records in the allocated state, this counter's own record included. |  |
| 1 | `counters.allocation_failed` | counter | static | Counter allocations refused because every record was in use: the counters file is full, and whatever needed the counter was refused with it. | The counters file is full and new publications and subscriptions are refused until a counter is freed: close what is not used; the capacity is fixed in this version. |
| 2 | `publication.position` | gauge | instance | The producer position of one publication's log buffer, written by the driver on its duty cycle from a load it makes at most once every two milliseconds, so at most two milliseconds behind the publisher (ADR 0022, ADR 0032); key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. |  |

| 76 | `receiver.setups_elicited` | counter | static | Status messages with the send-setup flag sent for a session with no record, asking the sender for its setup frame: a data datagram or heartbeat arrived for a wanted stream from a sender whose setups stopped before this receiver had a subscription, once per pending setup timeout (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 1). |  |
| 77 | `receiver.heartbeats_received` | counter | static | Heartbeats accepted for an image: the high-water mark follows them, and with EOS they name the end of stream (spec/udp.md, Heartbeat). |  |
| 78 | `receiver.status_messages_sent` | counter | static | Status messages sent for an image: one at its creation, then on the three triggers, the slowest reader a quarter window past the last, a window change, or the status message interval (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 4). |  |
| 79 | `receiver.naks_sent` | counter | static | NAKs sent for a gap: one after the NAK delay and one every NAK retry while the gap persists (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 3). | NAKs are loss being mended: a steady count under load is the network, the socket buffers or a sender that cannot keep up; compare sender.retransmits_sent on the sending host, and receiver.gaps_detected here; `cavalry doctor` names the image whose high-water mark runs ahead of its rebuild position. |
| 80 | `receiver.gaps_detected` | counter | static | Gaps first seen by the rebuild scan: a run of zero frame length words between the rebuild position and the next frame or the high-water mark, each a datagram lost or reordered on the wire (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 3). | Loss on the wire or in a socket buffer: a count that rises with receiver.naks_sent and sender.retransmits_sent is being mended; one that rises while image.rebuild_position stands still is a gap the sender no longer answers (sender.naks_ignored there) and the image will time out. |
| 81 | `receiver.under_runs` | counter | static | Data datagrams dropped because they began below the last status message's position: a late retransmit or a duplicate of what the subscribers have passed (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 2). |  |
| 82 | `receiver.over_runs` | counter | static | Data datagrams and heartbeats dropped because they ended more than half a term beyond the last status message's position: a sender past the window it was given (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 2). | A sender that ran more than half a term past the receiver's last status message: its status messages are not reaching it (sender.status_messages_received there) or it ignores the window; the dropped frames are NAKed once the status messages get through. |
| 83 | `receiver.rejected_datagrams` | counter | static | Data datagrams that failed the datagram check, dropped whole: a length not a multiple of 32, a frame that fails spec/frame.md's checks, a term offset that is not the running one, or frames past the end of the term (spec/udp.md, What a reader rejects). | A peer sending datagrams this version cannot read: check that both drivers run the same version; nothing of a rejected datagram is delivered. |
| 84 | `receiver.dropped_frames` | counter | static | Control frames and heartbeats a receive endpoint dropped because their version or type is not one this version reads, or they are too short (spec/udp.md, The datagram), and heartbeats whose term offset is not below their image's term length (spec/udp.md, What a reader rejects, term-offset). | A peer of another version, or something that is not Cavalry, sends to this endpoint's port, or a sender's heartbeats name a term offset past its image's term: check the peer's version and the port. |
| 85 | `receiver.dropped_pending` | counter | static | Setup frames, data datagrams and heartbeats dropped for a session pending a setup, the datagram that elicited the setup among them, with no status message sent for them (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 1). |  |
| 86 | `receiver.dropped_in_progress` | counter | static | Setup frames, data datagrams and heartbeats dropped for a session in progress, between the setup handed to the conductor and its image, or because the queue to the conductor had no room for the setup (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 1). | A conductor slow to create an image, under CPU throttling or a full counters file: a count that keeps rising for one session means the image is never created; look at driver.registry_full and driver.log_create_failed. |
| 87 | `receiver.dropped_cool_down` | counter | static | Setup frames, data datagrams and heartbeats dropped for a session on cool-down, the 10 s after its image was retired, so that a late frame creates no second image (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 5). | A sender that resumed after a pause of the liveness timeout, or a subscription added back on an endpoint that stayed open, waits up to one cool-down before the stream is received again; nothing to do unless the count keeps rising, which is a sender that paused for the timeout again. |
| 88 | `receiver.dropped_unwanted` | counter | static | Data datagrams, heartbeats and RTT measurements dropped for a stream no subscription on the endpoint wants, a datagram with EOS for a session with no record, an RTT measurement for a session with no image, or one for another receiver (spec/udp.md, The receiver, steps 1 and 6). |  |
| 89 | `receiver.sessions_full` | counter | static | Datagrams for a session with no record dropped because the session table held 4096 records, with no status message sent (spec/udp.md, The receiver). | More sessions than the table holds reach this driver, or senders that open a session per datagram: a record is freed when a pending setup expires, an image is refused or a cool-down ends, so the count stops once the senders do. |
| 90 | `receiver.rtt_replies_sent` | counter | static | RTT measurements with the reply flag answered for an image: the same frame without the flag, the echo timestamp and the receiver id unchanged (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 6). |  |
| 91 | `image.hwm_position` | gauge | instance | The high-water mark of one image: the highest position any accepted datagram or heartbeat reached, stored by the receiver with a release store; key: the image's registration id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian, as subscription.position; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. | An image.hwm_position that runs ahead of image.rebuild_position is a gap: receiver.gaps_detected and receiver.naks_sent say whether it is being mended; one that stands still while the sender's sender.position moves is a link that dropped everything. |
| 92 | `image.rebuild_position` | gauge | instance | The rebuild position of one image: the end of the contiguous frames from its start, the furthest a subscriber can read, stored by the receiver with a release store; key and label as image.hwm_position. | A rebuild position that stands still below the high-water mark is a gap the sender is not mending: sender.naks_ignored on the sending host says it fell outside the resend window; the image times out after the liveness timeout. |
| 93 | `image.created` | counter | static | Images created from a setup frame: the conductor made the log, allocated the counters and announced the image, and the receiver sent its first status message (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 1). |  |
| 94 | `image.ended` | counter | static | Images retired because their stream ended: a heartbeat with EOS named the end, the rebuild reached it, and every reader did too or the liveness timeout passed (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 5). |  |
| 95 | `image.timed_out` | counter | static | Images retired because no accepted datagram or heartbeat arrived for the image liveness timeout, 10 s (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 5). | The sender stopped, its host went away, or the link dropped everything for 10 s: the subscribers got unavailable image; a sender that comes back creates a new image after the cool-down. |
| 96 | `image.unsubscribed` | counter | static | Images retired because their last subscription on the endpoint and stream was removed, by remove subscription, client close or client timeout, with no unavailable image for a subscription its client removed (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 5). |  |
| 97 | `image.removed` | counter | static | Retired images whose log the conductor unlinked after unavailable image went to the subscriptions that remained and their counters were freed (spec/udp.md, The receiver, step 5). |  |
| 98 | `subscription.add_deferred` | counter | static | `add subscription` commands on a `cavalry:udp` channel whose previous receive endpoint was still closing, held with nothing registered until the receiver closed it and then run as if they had just arrived (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands; ADR 0049). |  |
| 99 | `subscription.add_deferred_timed_out` | counter | static | `add subscription` commands that waited the closing endpoint wait, 5 s, for a `cavalry:udp` channel's previous receive endpoint to close and were answered with code 4, with nothing registered; the close that came later ran nothing for them (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands, Liveness and timeouts; ADR 0049). | The receiver did not close a channel's previous receive endpoint within 5 s of an add on it, so the add was refused with code 4: the driver's receiver thread is behind, starved of CPU under a cgroup quota or busy; give the driver's threads the CPU they need, then add the subscription again. |
| 100 | `subscription.add_deferred_waiting` | gauge | static | `add subscription` commands waiting now for a `cavalry:udp` channel's previous receive endpoint to close, each holding a slot of the subscriptions registry until the close runs it, its client goes or the closing endpoint wait refuses it (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands, Sizes; ADR 0049). |  |
| 101 | `sender.flow_control_receivers_timed_out` | counter | static | Receivers dropped from a min publication's table for no status message within the flow control receiver timeout, 5 s; one dropped because its last status message carried end of stream, as every receiver's does after a clean close, is not counted; the sender limit then follows the slowest of the receivers that remain (spec/udp.md, The sender; ADR 0053, ADR 0054). | A destination whose driver stopped answering held the stream back for the timeout: check that its driver runs and that its subscription is live, or remove the destination with remove destination; sender.flow_control_receivers says how many answer now. |
| 102 | `sender.flow_control_receivers_full` | counter | static | Status messages from a receiver a min publication's full table of 64 does not hold: accepted for the connection and not tracked, so the sender limit does not follow that receiver (spec/udp.md, The sender; ADR 0053). | More than 64 receivers answered one min publication within 5 s, which 64 destinations never produce: a receiver that restarts draws a new receiver id each time, so a flapping destination fills the table; find it from its driver's image.created. |
| 103 | `sender.flow_control_receivers` | gauge | instance | The receivers in one cavalry:udp publication's min table, each answering within the flow control receiver timeout, and once the publication is closed each whose stream ended too, kept until the linger ends, so that a clean close leaves it at the receivers that took the stream to its end; 0 under max, which keeps no table; key as sender.position; label text: sender.position's four, then the publication's strategy as fc=max or fc=min, space-separated, so that doctor reads which publications keep a table (ADR 0053, ADR 0056). | A min publication whose receivers are fewer than its endpoint's channel.destinations has a destination that is not answering: the stream waits for it until the timeout drops it, then runs without it. |
| 104 | `channel.destinations` | gauge | instance | How many destinations one send endpoint of a control channel sends to, added with add destination and removed with remove destination; 0 on any other endpoint; key and label as channel.status (spec/udp.md, The sender; ADR 0053). | A control channel's endpoint with 0 destinations sends nothing: add one with add destination on a publication of the channel. |

## State machines

Every state machine on the data plane registers its states and transitions in `counters.toml` too, and `just lint-counters` fails a transition that names no counter, a counter that is not of kind `counter` in the table above, a counter whose constant no code in the enum's crate names, or an enum whose variants are not the machine's states (CLAUDE.md, invariant 4). The enum that holds the states carries the comment `// state machine: <name>` on the line before its definition. The check fails closed: every enum under `crates/*/src` whose name is or ends in `State`, `Status` or `Phase` carries that comment, or `// not a state machine: <why>` with the reason no transition of it needs a counter, and `just lint-counters` names the file and line of one that has neither. Each machine is listed here with the counter every transition adds one to.

### `counters_record`

States: `unused`, `allocated`, `reclaimed`.

| From | To | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unused` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `reclaimed` | `allocated` | `counters.allocations` |
| `allocated` | `reclaimed` | `counters.freed` |
